title: The Great Depression
examples: What caused the Great Depression to spread around the world?
How did the crash on Wall Street affect countries far away?
What major changes did governments make to fix the economy?

explain.say: Today we will learn about the Great Depression. This was a very difficult time for the world economy. We will look at what started it and how it spread.

First we look at the Wall Street Crash. This happened in October of nineteen twenty-nine. Many people bought and sold stocks very quickly. The sudden drop caused huge financial losses for many people.
Next we explore the global effects. When the US economy struggled, other countries felt the pinch. Trade slowed down everywhere, hurting many industries worldwide.
Then we examine the responses from governments. Leaders introduced new programs to help people and restart businesses. These efforts changed how governments managed money.
For a real-life example consider a local shop. If the main high street shops close, the local bakery will also suffer. This shows how one business affects many others.

items: High Street: Main source of income
Local Bakery: Depends on foot traffic

explain.say: The most common mistake is thinking the crash was only about stocks. It was much deeper, affecting jobs, farms, and international trade too. Remember the whole system was connected.

faq.q: Why did the Great Depression start with the stock market?
faq.a: The crash signaled deep problems in the economy. It showed that the bubble of easy credit and speculation had burst. It was a symptom, not the sole cause.
asks: Was the stock market the only cause?
What did the crash really mean?

faq.q: How did the global economy react to the US crash?
faq.a: Nations relied on trade with the US. When US demand dropped, other countries lost their main buyers. This caused a worldwide drop in goods and services.

faq.q: What did the New Deal actually do for people?
faq.a: The New Deal introduced direct government aid. It created jobs in infrastructure like roads and dams. It changed the relationship between citizens and the state.
asks: Did the government just give out money?
What kind of help did Roosevelt give?

faq.q: Was the Depression solved by the New Deal alone?
faq.a: It provided crucial relief and reform. However, the Second World War is generally considered the major factor that ended the Great Depression. War spending revived global trade.
asks: Was it fully fixed by the New Deal?
Did the war end the Depression?

faq.a: Speculation means buying assets hoping the price will rise quickly. Many people bought stocks just because others were buying them, which is risky.
asks: Is it good to buy based on hype?

facts: The crash occurred in October of nineteen twenty-nine.
Global trade significantly decreased during the nineteen thirties.
The New Deal introduced federal programs for relief and recovery.
Mass unemployment was a defining feature of the period.

quiz.say: The initial trigger for the global downturn was:

options.show: D) A sudden rise in oil prices
options.say: D) A sudden rise in oil prices

quiz.why: The sudden collapse of stock prices signaled deep financial instability.

wrong.0: Oil prices were not the primary cause cited for the initial collapse.
wrong.2: While farming struggled, the crash was the immediate financial trigger.
wrong.3: Tariffs worsened it, but the crash started the cycle.

options.show: C) Reduced demand for goods everywhere
options.say: C) Reduced demand for goods everywhere

quiz.why: When money was scarce, people bought less, affecting all markets.

wrong.1: Investment dried up because people feared losing money.
wrong.2: Nations often devalued their currency, weakening exchange rates.
wrong.3: Commodity prices fell sharply due to lack of buyers.

quiz.say: A government response aimed at job creation was:
quiz.show: A) Increasing taxes on the wealthy

options.show: A) Increasing taxes on the wealthy
options.say: A) Increasing taxes on the wealthy

quiz.why: Public works, like roads, directly employed large numbers of people.

wrong.0: Lowering rates alone did not guarantee businesses would reopen.
wrong.1: This would have worsened the global economic situation.
wrong.3: While taxes were used, direct job creation was the main focus of relief.
